## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of circular shifts vs normal shifts and edge-case handling in a 32-bit width.

## Key Concepts
- Circular shifts vs arithmetic/logical shifts
- Width-aware masking and edge-cases
- Pure bitwise operations with no loops

## Code Example
```javascript
static inline uint32_t rotateRight32(uint32_t n, uint32_t k){
  k %= 32;
  return (n >> k) | (n << (32 - k));
}
```

- How would you adapt this for 64-bit inputs? 
- What changes if 0 < k < 64 is required?

## Why This Is Asked
This checks understanding of 128-bit bit rotations using only shifts and masks, with a branch-free formula.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and modulo wrap-around
- 128-bit arithmetic and safe shifts
- Branch-free expression design

## Code Example
```c
uint128 rotateRight128(uint128 x, uint64_t r){
  r &= 127; // 0..127
  return (x >> r) | (x << ((128 - r) % 128));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for rotate left? 
- What happens if r is large or negative input?
